canonical_statement: The review aimed to synthesize clinical outcomes and adverse events associated with triple therapy (ICS, LABA, and LAMA) versus dual therapy (ICS plus LABA) in children and adults with persistent uncontrolled moderate-to-severe asthma.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: To systematically synthesize the outcomes and adverse events associated with triple therapy (ICS, LABA, and LAMA) vs dual therapy (ICS plus LABA) in children and adults with persistent uncontrolled asthma.

canonical_statement: Eligible studies were randomized clinical trials of any duration or design comparing ICS/LABA/LAMA triple therapy with ICS/LABA dual therapy in patients with moderate-to-severe asthma.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: randomized clinical trials (RCTs) of any duration and design comparing triple therapy (ICS, LABA, plus LAMA) with dual therapy (ICS plus LABA) in patients with moderate to severe asthma

population.label: Eligible trial populations
inclusion_criteria: randomized comparison of triple vs dual therapy

canonical_statement: Observational and preclinical studies and studies limited to chronic respiratory diseases other than asthma were excluded.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Observational and preclinical studies and those limited to patients with chronic respiratory diseases other than asthma were excluded.

population.label: Excluded study populations/designs
exclusion_criteria: chronic respiratory disease other than asthma

canonical_statement: Triple therapy consisted of inhaled corticosteroid plus long-acting beta2-agonist plus long-acting muscarinic antagonist.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: triple therapy (ICS,LABA, plus LAMA)

exposures.details: Triple inhaler therapy; included tiotropium, umeclidinium, and/or glycopyrronium across trials.

canonical_statement: Severe asthma exacerbation was defined as requiring systemic corticosteroids for at least 3 days, hospitalization, intensive care admission or intubation, or an emergency department visit.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Severe asthma exacerbation was defined by a need for systemic steroids for 3 or more days, hospitalization, intensive care admission or intubation, or emergency department visits

outcome.definition: Need for systemic steroids for ≥3 days, hospitalization, intensive care admission/intubation, or emergency department visit

canonical_statement: Asthma control outcomes combined ACQ-5, ACQ-6, ACQ-7, and ACT scores using standardized mean differences; pooled effects were converted to the ACQ-7 scale for interpretability.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: scores for ACQ versions 5, 6, 7, and the ACT were pooled together using standardized mean difference (SMD)... converted these pooled SMDs to... ACQ-7

outcome.measurement_method: ACQ-5/6/7 or ACT pooled as SMD and back-converted to ACQ-7

canonical_statement: Asthma-related quality of life was measured using AQLQ or Mini-AQLQ and pooled using standardized mean differences; the minimal important difference for both instruments was 0.5.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: For quality-of-life measures, the AQLQ and Mini-AQLQ were pooled using SMD... The minimal important difference for a change in both AQLQ and Mini-AQLQ is 0.5.

outcome.measurement_method: AQLQ or Mini-AQLQ pooled as SMD

canonical_statement: Lung function was assessed using trough FEV1 in liters; the review noted a generally accepted minimal important difference of 100 to 200 mL or 15% to 20%, although a definitive threshold was not established.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: For FEV1, although the minimal important difference is not definitively established, generally accepted minimal important difference in the literature is 100 to 200 mL or change of 15% to 20%.

outcome.measurement_method: Forced expiratory volume in 1 second, liters

canonical_statement: The search covered MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL, the WHO International Clinical Trials Registry, FDA, and EMA sources from November 2017 through December 8, 2020, without language restriction.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL, ICTRP, FDA, and EMA databases from November 2017, to December 8, 2020, without language restriction.

canonical_statement: Two investigators independently screened titles/abstracts and full texts, with disagreements resolved by consensus.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Two investigators ... independently screened titles and abstracts... Similarly, 2 investigators ... independently reviewed full-text articles. Disagreements were resolved through consensus.

canonical_statement: Two investigators independently extracted data using a prepiloted standardized form, and paired investigators independently assessed risk of bias using Cochrane RoB 2.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Two investigators ... independently extracted data using a prepiloted standardized form... Paired investigators ... independently assessed risk of bias using version 2 of the Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials (RoB 2).

canonical_statement: Primary meta-analyses used DerSimonian-Laird random-effects models; heterogeneity was assessed visually and with I2, and publication bias was assessed using the GRADE approach including funnel-plot inspection.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: DerSimonian and Laird random-effects models were used for the primary meta-analyses... Heterogeneity was assessed... quantified with I2... Publication bias was assessed using the GRADE approach... visually inspecting funnel plots

canonical_statement: The certainty of evidence for each outcome was evaluated with GRADE and trial sequential analysis was used as an objective measure of optimal information size and imprecision.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: To evaluate the certainty (quality) of evidence for each outcome, the GRADE approach was used with trial sequential analysis as an objective measure of optimal information size and imprecision.

canonical_statement: For time-to-first severe exacerbation, the review digitized published Kaplan-Meier curves, reconstructed patient-level data, validated proportional-hazards assumptions, and fitted a shared-frailty Cox model with study as a random effect.

canonical_statement: Prespecified subgroup analyses examined risk of bias, exacerbation history, smoking history, age, intervention/comparator dose and type, and type-2 inflammatory phenotype; sensitivity analyses addressed missing data, fixed effects, unpublished studies, crossover trials, dose handling, alternative random-effects estimation, and correlation assumptions.
